title: Fog Nodes and Orchestration — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature-grade methods developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout. How fog nodes are provisioned, scheduled, and orchestrated as one coherent fleet. Fog nodes — gateways, on-prem servers, smart routers, roadside units, micro data centers — form a heterogeneous, geographically spread fleet. Orchestration provisions workloads onto them: service discovery, placement under latency and capacity constraints, scaling, migration on node failure, and lifecycle management. Because nodes differ in CPU, memory, accelerators, and connectivity, placement is a constrained optimization problem, often solved with heuristics or lightweight schedulers adapted from cloud orchestrators to the edge. Signature method: Signature Two-Pass Placement: coarse pass by latency ring, fine pass by resource fit, with a deterministic tie-break so placements are reproducible across runs.
